title: Trentino-Alto Adige's Pumps Ease Into Mid-November as Methane Pulls Away From Every Other Fuel
dek: Petrol and diesel drift slightly lower across the region while methane prices climb to an 18% premium over the national average.
executive_summary: Trentino-Alto Adige enters the week with petrol and diesel both inching down day over day — self-service Benzina at €2.0110/L (-0.08%) and Gasolio at €2.2565/L (-0.06%) — while GPL and Metano held perfectly flat versus yesterday at €0.8366/L and €2.4990/L respectively. Against today's national self-service averages (Benzina €1.9734, Gasolio €2.2371, GPL €0.828, Metano €2.1125), the region is running richer on all four fuels, most sharply on methane, where the local price sits a full 18.3% above the national figure.

Zoom out to the weekly data tracked since late July, though, and one fuel dwarfs the other three: regional Metano has climbed roughly 39% since the week of 2026-07-20, against a 41% national rise, while Benzina is essentially flat (-0.5% regionally) and Gasolio is up only a few percent. GPL is the fuel worth watching most closely right now — it has risen more slowly here than nationally over the full period, and in the most recent two tracked weeks the two lines actually split direction, with the region easing back just as the national average kept climbing.

fuel_sections.heading: Petrol Holds Just Above €2 as the Region Underperforms a National Near-Flatline
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Trentino-Alto Adige priced at €2.0110/L today, down €0.0016 (-0.08%) from yesterday's €2.0126 — essentially unchanged. That's €0.0376 (+1.9%) above today's national self-service average of €1.9734/L, a premium that has held fairly steady through the week.

Looking at the full tracked window, regional Benzina has actually slipped from €2.021/L in the week of 2026-07-20 to €2.0118/L in the week of 2026-11-09, a net -0.46%, after peaking at €2.2085/L in the week of 2026-09-21. Nationally the round trip was milder: €1.9756 to €1.9744 (-0.06%), off an identical September peak of €2.1669. In other words, the region rose and fell by roughly the same amount as the rest of Italy, but has slipped a little further below its starting point on the way back down.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Cools From Its September Peak, Region Still Running a Touch Above the Nation
paragraphs: Self-service Gasolio priced at €2.2565/L today, down €0.0013 (-0.06%) from yesterday's €2.2578, versus a national self-service average of €2.2371/L today — the region sits €0.0194 (+0.87%) richer.

The multi-week shape mirrors Benzina closely: regional diesel climbed from €2.2063/L in the week of 2026-07-20 to a peak of €2.4048/L in the week of 2026-09-21, then eased back to €2.2572/L by the week of 2026-11-09 — a net +2.31% over the full span and a -6.14% retreat from the peak. Nationally the pattern tracks almost step for step: €2.1747 to a same-week peak of €2.3736, settling at €2.2376 (+2.89% net, -5.73% off peak). The region's September run-up and subsequent pullback have both been marginally sharper than the rest of the country's.

fuel_sections.heading: LPG Is the One Fuel Pulling in Two Different Directions Right Now
paragraphs: Self-service GPL priced at €0.8366/L today, unchanged from yesterday, and €0.0086 (+1.04%) above today's national self-service average of €0.828/L.

Over the full tracked window, regional GPL is up 5.74% (from €0.7912/L in the week of 2026-07-20 to €0.8366/L in the week of 2026-11-09), while the national figure rose a steeper 9.06% (€0.7592 to €0.828) over the same span — the rest of Italy has been closing the gap on what is usually a regionally pricier fuel here. More notable still: in the two most recent tracked weeks the lines diverged outright. Trentino-Alto Adige's GPL actually eased back from a €0.8452/L high in the week of 2026-11-02 to €0.8366/L the following week (-1.0%), while the national average kept climbing from €0.7994 to €0.828 (+3.6%) over that same stretch — the clearest cross-fuel divergence in this report.

fuel_sections.heading: Methane Keeps Rising — Up Roughly 39% Since Tracking Began, Now 18% Above the National Average
paragraphs: Self-service Metano priced at €2.499/L today in Trentino-Alto Adige, unchanged from yesterday, and now €0.3865 (+18.3%) above today's national self-service average of €2.1125/L — by far the widest regional premium of any fuel covered in this report. One oddity worth flagging: the region's self-service price (€2.499) currently sits above its own full-service price (€2.1947), an inversion of the usual self-service discount seen across the other three fuels here.

Zoomed out, Metano is the story of the entire tracked period: regional prices have climbed from €1.7993/L in the week of 2026-07-20 to €2.499/L by the week of 2026-11-09 — a 38.9% increase with no sustained pullback along the way. Nationally the climb has been even steeper in percentage terms, from €1.4999 to €2.1132 (+40.9%), albeit from a lower starting base. No other fuel in this report has moved anywhere close to this magnitude; Benzina and Gasolio have shifted by low single digits over the same four months.

network_section.heading: 389 Registered Stations, 369 Reporting — A Tighter Network Than the National Average
paragraphs: Trentino-Alto Adige currently counts 389 registered filling stations, of which 369 reported a price today — a 94.9% reporting rate. That compares with 21,666 of 23,960 stations reporting nationally, a 90.4% rate, meaning the region's network is, proportionally, more consistently represented in the daily data than Italy as a whole.

The registered count has been essentially flat across the tracked period: 390 stations on 2026-07-21, dipping as low as 387 in early November before recovering to 389 by mid-November. That pattern looks more like small administrative churn — stations briefly dropping off the registry and reappearing — than genuine openings or closures.

methodology_section.heading: Built, Not Written: How This Report Updates Itself Every Day
paragraphs: This entire report — the underlying price data, the weekly trend analysis above, the choice of Trentino-Alto Adige as today's spotlight region, and the prose itself — is generated automatically every day by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. Each morning the pipeline pulls the latest station and price data from Italy's MIMIT feed, rotates deterministically through the country's 20 regions so every region gets its turn, computes a week-by-week trend for all four tracked fuels against the national average, and writes up the findings without a human drafting a single sentence.

Contrast that with the alternative: a manually-maintained spreadsheet that someone has to remember to download, clean, and re-chart every day, with trend analysis limited to whatever a person has time to compute by hand. The pipeline behind this report does that work unattended, consistently, at a scale and regularity a manual process can't easily match.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Trentino-Alto Adige
paragraphs: The live Fuel Dashboard opens by default on Agip Eni's brand-level view — but that's just the starting point. Use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality, or another Operator/Brand entirely, and explore how today's numbers for Trentino-Alto Adige compare to wherever you're reading this from.

caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight region is Trentino-Alto Adige — and the number that stands out is methane. Regional Metano prices have climbed roughly 39% since tracking began in late July, and today sit about 18% above Italy's national average, by far the widest premium of any fuel in the dataset. Petrol and diesel, by contrast, are essentially flat to slightly down day over day.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, self-updating interactive dashboard that tracks petrol, diesel, LPG and methane prices across every region, province, municipality and operator in Italy, refreshed daily from the Ministry's own MIMIT feed. No one opens a spreadsheet to do this — a small unattended pipeline built with Claude Code pulls the data, rotates through Italy's 20 regions for a daily spotlight, computes the weekly trends, and writes the report you're reading right now, every single day without manual intervention.

That's the real pitch here: a few years ago this would have meant a manually-maintained Excel file, updated whenever someone remembered to. Today it's a live interactive site plus a fresh, data-grounded written report, generated end-to-end by AI tooling. Check out the dashboard at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/ and explore today's Trentino-Alto Adige numbers for yourself.
